name: Inverse trig and integration formulas
about: From the revision sheet. 21 cards, one fact each. Left out on purpose: anything you can derive in seconds (power rule, ∫sin, ∫cos, ∫eˣ, ∫sec²).

cards.front: Sketch y = sin⁻¹ x. Mark the endpoints and the origin.
cards.back: Domain [−1, 1], range [−π/2, π/2]. Odd, increasing, vertical at ±1.

cards.front: Sketch y = cos⁻¹ x. Mark the endpoints and the middle point.
cards.back: Domain [−1, 1], range [0, π]. Decreasing. cos⁻¹x = π/2 − sin⁻¹x.

cards.front: Sketch y = tan⁻¹ x. Mark the asymptotes.
cards.back: Domain all x, range (−π/2, π/2). Odd, increasing, flattens to ±π/2.

cards.front: Sketch y = sec⁻¹ x. Which values of x exist, and what is the one y it never reaches?
cards.back: |x| ≥ 1, range [0, π] without π/2. Two branches, both increasing.

cards.front: Power-reduction identities for sin²x and cos²x?

cards.back: x = a sin θ, because 1 − sin²θ = cos²θ
x = a tan θ, because 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ
x = a sec θ, because sec²θ − 1 = tan²θ

cards.front: Integration by parts: how to choose u?
cards.back: LIATE: Log, Inverse trig, Algebraic, Trig, Exponential. The earliest in the list is u.

cards.front: In a double integral the inner integral is ∫ e^(x²) dx (or sin x / x). What now?
cards.back: No elementary antiderivative. Sketch the region and swap the order of integration.
